reason: The passage describes Israel (יִשְׂרָאֵל) as a cohesive military force engaged in organized warfare with the Amalekites. The text portrays them as 'עַם' (people/nation) with structured military hierarchy—Joshua commands selected men, Moses and other leaders coordinate strategy—organized enough to prevail in sustained combat. The reference to warfare 'from generation to generation' (מִדֹּר דֹּֽר) indicates a nations-level conflict, not a family or religious community. While their relationship with Yahweh frames the narrative, Israel is clearly depicted here in their political and military capacity as a national entity, extending well beyond familial bonds or mere religious adherence.
